**Root Cause: Liveness probe is killing the pods before shard loading finishes — triggered by a larger index snapshot, not a code change.**

**What the evidence shows:**

Both pods (`catalog-search-7d6f9b8c5-4kxpw`, 11 restarts; `catalog-search-7d6f9b8c5-s9m2t`, 10 restarts) are in `CrashLoopBackOff` with exit code 143 (SIGTERM).

The application logs show the exact failure pattern on every restart:
```
INFO index snapshot catalog-2026-05-12T03 has 48 shards (12.4 GiB), loading into memory before opening HTTP listener
INFO loaded shard 4/48
...
INFO loaded shard 20/48  (or 23/48)
INFO received SIGTERM, aborting shard load
INFO shutdown complete
```

The HTTP listener on port 8080 only opens **after all 48 shards are loaded**. Each shard takes ~9 seconds, meaning full startup requires roughly **~430 seconds (~7 minutes)**. However, the current liveness probe is configured with `initialDelaySeconds=30`, `period=10s`, and `failureThreshold=3`, which means Kubernetes kills the container if port 8080 is not responding within **60 seconds** of startup (30s delay + 3 × 10s). The pod always gets killed mid-load (at shard ~20–23 of 48), which causes the SIGTERM and the restart loop.

This worked fine last week because the index was smaller and loaded fast enough to pass the probe. Today's snapshot (`catalog-2026-05-12T03`) grew to **48 shards / 12.4 GiB**, pushing startup time well beyond the probe's tolerance — no code change needed to trigger this.

**The Fix: Add a `startupProbe` to the Deployment**

The recommended approach for slow-starting containers is to add a `startupProbe` that checks the same endpoint. Kubernetes will not run the liveness probe until the startup probe succeeds, giving the app time to finish initialization [cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes#define-startup-probes-0][cite: concepts/workloads/pods/probes#when-should-you-use-a-startup-probe-0].

Add the following `startupProbe` to the `catalog-search` container spec in the Deployment:

```yaml
startupProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /healthz
    port: 8080
  failureThreshold: 60   # 60 × 10s = 600s max startup window (covers ~430s load + headroom)
  periodSeconds: 10
```

Leave the existing `livenessProbe` unchanged — once the startup probe succeeds, the liveness probe takes over as normal to detect deadlocks [cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-liveness-readiness-startup-probes#define-startup-probes-1].

**Summary of action:** Edit the `catalog-search` Deployment, add the `startupProbe` block above to the container spec, and apply the change. The pods will be replaced and should complete startup successfully. If the index continues to grow, consider tuning `failureThreshold` upward or investigating whether the app can open the HTTP listener before shards are fully loaded.
